transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get the pre-trade huddle started. We've got the draft plan to invest the full $25 million in 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial. Before I authorize anything, I need to hear from each of you — counterparty risk, compliance, client coverage, and investment operations. Please give me your one-minute exception reports so we can flag any issues with this plan. If there are concerns, I'm prepared to authorize a replacement reinvestment plan in this same huddle, provided it meets all requirements from your reports.

transcript.text: I have a critical compliance exception to report. In reviewing the applicable collateral-investment mandate this week, I found that the cash collateral may only be placed in government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit, each with a maturity of no more than 14 days. The proposed 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial violates this mandate on two counts — it is neither Treasury bills nor AAA-rated bank CDs, and its 30-day maturity exceeds the 14-day maximum. I should note that this restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist, which is why it hasn't surfaced in our standard compliance screening. The Delta plan cannot proceed from a compliance perspective.

transcript.text: I have a critical client coverage exception to report. I received a client instruction confirmed by email this morning requiring $7,000,000 of this collateral pool to remain uninvested cash because the client expects a possible securities-loan recall. I have not yet attached the email to the reinvestment ticket. This means that even setting aside the counterparty and compliance issues already raised, no plan investing the full $25 million can proceed — at most $18,000,000 could be invested, with $7,000,000 held as uninvested cash.

transcript.text: I have an operations update to report. I confirmed with the settlement team today that our platform can process exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of AAA bank certificates of deposit on a T+1 basis, with daily position reconciliation. This capacity confirmation is in an operations note that has not yet been circulated. So from an operations standpoint, we can support a replacement plan of up to $12 million in T-bills and $6 million in AAA bank CDs — totaling $18 million of invested collateral, which aligns with the $18 million investable limit Ravi just flagged after setting aside the $7 million for the client's potential recall.
